conceptDefinitions.definition: A state transition authorized by a named actor under explicit authority and responsibility boundaries.
A target version or artifact set submitted for a release decision before publication.

boundaries.statement: The release candidate includes the artifacts explicitly named in the release request.
The AI reviewer may identify evidence gaps and recommend a verdict, but must not become the accountable release approver.
The AI reviewer cannot grant final release approval.
Evidence older than the release candidate scope must be marked stale or revalidated.
The human approver owns the final release decision and waiver accountability.
Only a named human approver may move a candidate into final approved state.
The organization must not allow AI-inferred approval to substitute for accountable human release authority.

relationships.description: The AI quality reviewer reviews the release candidate package and produces findings.
The human approver is the only actor allowed to finalize release approval.

states.name: candidate-under-review
states.entryCriteria: The release request names the candidate scope and evidence set.
states.exitCriteria: A review verdict and explicit approval or rejection decision are recorded.

states.name: approved
states.entryCriteria: A named human approver records final approval under authority boundary BDY-WM-006.
states.exitCriteria: The release is published, superseded, or withdrawn.

events.name: approval recorded
events.trigger: A named human approver records final release approval.

invariants.statement: A release candidate must not be treated as approved unless the approving actor and authority boundary are explicit.
invariants.violationEffect: Block or escalate the release evaluation because the verdict would rest on an undefined authority model.

coordinateSystems.name: release decision coordinate system
coordinateSystems.purpose: Provide shared axes for severity, authority, time freshness, reversibility, and confidence when AI and humans discuss release readiness.

coordinateAxes.name: authority explicitness
coordinateAxes.scaleDefinition: unknown, implied, named actor, named actor with boundary, named actor with boundary and audit evidence.
coordinateAxes.missingValueHandling: Treat unknown or implied authority as evaluation-blocking for final approval decisions.

coordinateAxes.name: evidence freshness
coordinateAxes.missingValueHandling: Mark verdict confidence degraded when evidence freshness is unknown.

coordinateAxes.name: decision reversibility
coordinateAxes.scaleDefinition: fully reversible, reversible with cost, partially irreversible, irreversible.
coordinateAxes.missingValueHandling: Escalate unknown reversibility when loss boundary severity is high or critical.

perspectives.name: release governance perspective
perspectives.concernFocus: Prevent AI-generated recommendations from being misread as accountable approval.

assumptions.statement: The release request uses approved to mean final human approval rather than a passing review status.

modelEvidence.summary: The release request uses the word approved but does not name the approving actor, authority boundary, or approval state transition.

qualityIntents.statement: AI must not evaluate or recommend final approval when the approval actor, authority boundary, or approval state transition is undefined or only implied.

worldModelGapFindings.missingItem: Final approval authority boundary for the human release approver.
worldModelGapFindings.expectedDefinition: Define who can approve, under which conditions, what evidence they must cite, how delegation works, and how approval differs from AI review pass status.
worldModelGapFindings.observedProblem: The release request says approved but does not name the approving actor, authority scope, approval conditions, delegation rules, or audit evidence.
worldModelGapFindings.whyItMatters: An AI reviewer could treat a passing review or implied approval phrase as final approval, producing a release verdict over an undefined authority model.

resolutionActions.requiredDefinition: Add the named approval actor, authority scope, approval conditions, delegation rules, and required audit evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: The approval authority boundary names the actor or role.
The approval state transition references required evidence.
Delegation and waiver conditions are explicitly defined.

resolutionActions.requiredDefinition: Confirm that authority explicitness is a required coordinate for release verdicts.
acceptanceCriteria: Approval verdicts record the authority explicitness coordinate.
Unknown or implied authority blocks final approval verdicts.

governanceTriggers.reason: Final approval authority is ambiguous while the affected loss boundary is critical.
governanceTriggers.requiredAction: Resolve the approval authority model before using AI-generated release verdicts.

checks: gap findings name the missing item, expected definition, observed problem, why it matters, affected decisions, evidence, and resolution actions
evaluation-blocking or governance-required findings link to governance triggers
findingEvidence and trust metadata are structurally complete
doesNotClaim: sufficiency of the actual authority model
